meta.title: Operation of Hammer Mill in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To reduce the particle size of hard, fibrous, and tough crude drugs including bark, roots, seeds, and woody stems using high-speed rotating hammers for preparation of uniform coarse to medium powders.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for primary size reduction of hard crude drugs that cannot be processed by a simple mechanical grinder, prior to Soxhlet extraction or powder standardization.
procedure: Inspect the hammer mill chamber, hammers, screen, and feed hopper for cleanliness and absence of residue from previous use.
Select and fit the appropriate perforated screen at the discharge outlet: large holes (3–5 mm) for coarse reduction; medium holes (1–2 mm) for moderate reduction.
Ensure the crude drug material is dry — moisture above 10% causes jamming.
Pre-cut large pieces of drug material (bark, roots) to fragments < 5 cm using cutting tools before loading the hammer mill.
Ensure the collection vessel (bag or tray) is properly fitted at the discharge outlet.
Switch on the hammer mill motor and allow it to reach full operating speed before feeding material (approximately 10 seconds).
Feed the drug material slowly and continuously into the feed hopper in small handfuls — do not dump large quantities at once.
Monitor the motor current/sound — if the motor strains or slows, reduce the feed rate.
Collect the discharged powder in a clean, labelled container.
After all material is processed, allow the mill to run for 30 seconds empty to discharge remaining material.
Switch off the mill and wait for all moving parts to stop completely before opening.
Remove the screen and clean the chamber with a compressed air jet, then a soft brush.
Sieve the collected powder through the appropriate IP sieve to verify particle size and remove any unground pieces.
Weigh and label the final powder with drug name, particle size range, and date.
Record batch weight, screen size, and powder yield in the logbook.
precautions: Never insert hands or any object into the feed hopper while the mill is running.
Wear a dust mask (N95), safety goggles, and hearing protection — hammer mills generate significant dust and noise.
Do not process wet or oil-rich materials — they clog the screen and cause heat buildup.
Wait for complete stop before opening the chamber — hammers continue spinning after switch-off.
Inspect hammers and screen for wear before each batch — worn hammers reduce efficiency and produce inconsistent particle sizes.
Ground the equipment to prevent static charge accumulation when processing fine powders.
Never process stones, metal fragments, or non-drug material — foreign objects damage the hammers and screen at high speed.
Clean thoroughly between different drug materials to prevent cross-contamination.
